UK officer discusses allowing transgender men and women to serve in armed forces
I'm hoping this becomes the norm. I served 10 years before my transition and I don't believe it would have any impact on how I did my job.

Correct me if I'm wrong, but isn't one of the hurdles of having transgender people serve in the military the fact that hormones are a medication that are required to be taken regularly, and if you are required to regularly take a specific medication you're not allowed to serve to do accessibility issues? I haven't done a lot of research into hormone treatments, but I suppose if there's no negative side effects involving having to come off of them, then there shouldn't be an issue.

You're right, they would have to stock hormones and I'm not sure if they already stock them now or not. It's certainly not a big hurdle to overcome. Going off hormones for a trans woman is like reaching menopause.

I had a discussion with some active duty military about transgender military service. The point that seemed most effective in changing their minds was that the medical needs of cis woman were just as great as trans women, but trans women can't get pregnant.

I hadn't realized ciswomen are allowed birth control while serving until you mentioned it. I suppose that's a fair comparison, though I don't know how equal the effects of going off birth control and going off hormones are. It really comes down to how badly the withdrawls would be if by some unfortunate event cut off the supply and a soldier would have to operate without it.

As a bit of a side note, it's also important to remember in that argument that ciswomen don't necessarily just use birth control to avoid pregnancies. Many use it to fix hormonal issues, and reduce the severity/frequency of periods. Which I think is important to remember because it points out that the pill has legitimate medical benefits outside of contraceptive uses. So that could support your argument.
